prerequisites: Technological, economic, and IT knowledge from industrial engineering training acquired in the first-level degree.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the configuration of a utility system.
Know the main components and their fields of application.
Perform sizing and make the optimal technical-economic choice of the main elements present in a service plant.
Identify the most suitable elements for configuring a utility system based on the specified needs of the users.
Evaluate the technical feasibility of a system design.
Compare different system alternatives based on economic and reliability parameters.
Describe, in writing, in a clear and concise manner, and to present orally with appropriate language the objectives, procedure, and results of the analysis conducted.
Apply the knowledge acquired to contexts different from those presented during the course, such as, for example, DIME service facilities.
Develop the main components of a project plan.
Establish a control system necessary for the execution phase of any project.
Effectively analyze and manage project risks.
Correctly evaluate the technical, economic, and financial aspects of a new industrial initiative.
Plan project activities with a focus on time and cost scheduling.
Properly monitor their execution in accordance with existing constraints.
Identify a project's critical activities, the necessary resources, and the constraints present during the planning phase.
Assess the status of a project during the execution phase.
Describe, in writing, in a clear and concise manner, and to present orally, using appropriate language, the objectives, procedures, and results of the work performed.
Apply the knowledge acquired to contexts different from those presented during the course, such as projects of different scales or complexity, or related to industrial and non-industrial cases.

syllabus_topics: Factors in the selection of plant facility systems: costs, reliability, and efficiency of components and systems
Systems for the supply, storage, treatment, and distribution of industrial water
Compressed air production and distribution systems
Thermal energy production and distribution systems
Electric power transformation and distribution systems
assessment_rules: Learning outcomes for both modules will be assessed through a written exam and an oral exam. The final grade is the arithmetic mean of the marks obtained in the written test and the oral exam. A sufficient mark (18 out of 30) is given to a single question when the student shows elementary but adequate knowledge. Honors will be awarded with a maximum mark and demonstrated readiness in connecting topics and in-depth knowledge beyond course content.
